questions.q: What best describes the core difference between monitoring and observability?
options: Monitoring is for small apps, observability is for large ones
Monitoring watches for known failure modes; observability lets you investigate problems nobody predicted
They are two marketing names for the same tool
Observability is just monitoring with more dashboards
questions.explain: Monitoring answers questions you already knew to ask (known unknowns). Observability is a system property that lets you answer novel questions (unknown unknowns) using data the system already emits.

questions.q: A 'known unknown' in this lesson's terminology refers to:
options: A failure mode you anticipated and already built a check for
A bug that has never happened before
A metric nobody is collecting
An outage with no root cause
questions.explain: A known unknown is something you know you need to watch for, even though you don't know exactly when it will happen — like Northbridge's database connection pool running out.

questions.q: Why did observability become necessary as architectures moved toward microservices?
options: Microservices are slower, so more alerts are needed
The number of possible failure combinations grows too large to pre-build a dashboard for every one
Monitoring tools stopped working on containers
Microservices don't produce logs
questions.explain: With dozens of independently deployed, autoscaled services and third-party dependencies, you can't anticipate every failure mode in advance — you need the ability to investigate novel problems after the fact.

questions.q: Northbridge Retail's checkout service sees a latency spike during a flash sale caused by one product's image CDN timing out for mobile users in one region. Why is this an 'unknown unknown'?
options: Because nobody had pre-built a dashboard panel for that exact combination of conditions
Because CDNs never fail
Because it only affected one user
Because it was caused by a code deploy
questions.explain: Nobody anticipated that exact narrow combination of conditions in advance, so there was no pre-built alert for it — discovering it requires an observable system, not just monitoring.

questions.q: Which statement about monitoring and observability is most accurate?
options: Observability replaces monitoring entirely; you no longer need alerts on known thresholds
They serve complementary purposes — monitoring for known failure modes, observability for everything else
Monitoring is a subset of observability with no distinct purpose
Observability only applies to logs, not metrics or traces
questions.explain: Monitoring still matters for known failure modes you want to be paged on immediately. Observability extends your ability to investigate what monitoring alone can't anticipate.
